title: MSCI Emerging Markets Exit Risks Up to $11B in Indonesia
summary: MSCI may move Indonesia out of MSCI Emerging Markets to Standalone status, with up to $11B of foreign funds at stake. What it means for EIDO, EEM and VWO.
body_markdown:
## How Much Foreign Money Has Left and Could Leave: BI’s Figure and Analyst Estimates


Destry Damayanti of Bank Indonesia said the stock market saw a foreign outflow of US$0.9 billion in the fourth quarter through November 16, 2026, even as total flows showed a US$4.8 billion net inflow supported by global sukuk, government global bonds and government bonds (SBN),[as reported by detikFinance](https://finance.detik.com/bursa-dan-valas/d-8758539/modal-asing-masuk-ri-us-4-8-miliar-tapi-pasar-saham-tekor-us-900-juta) . She tied the swings to global uncertainty and foreign investor sentiment in the stock market.


Mirae’s estimate is far larger, and its baseline scenario is a move to Standalone. Using foreign-ownership data from Indonesia’s central securities depository (KSEI) through October 2026, it sees US$8 billion to US$11 billion of foreign funds potentially affected, of which about US$3 billion could actually leave, according to[Kumparan](https://kumparan.com/kumparanbisnis/rupiah-berpotensi-tembus-rp-19-000-per-dolar-as-msci-arus-modal-asing-jadi-tekanan-28aeYEXl1i9) . Mirae called the figures a research estimate of risk, not a forecast of certain outflows, and Rully said the rupiah could weaken toward Rp19,000 per US dollar in 2027.

## Indonesia’s Regulator Responds: 18 Meetings With MSCI


OJK chair Friderica Widyasari Dewi said the Financial Services Authority (OJK) and the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) have met MSCI one-on-one 18 times since January 2026 and briefed more than 1,000 global investors,[as reported by Liputan6](https://www.liputan6.com/saham/read/8337410/reformasi-pasar-modal-ojk-gelar-18-pertemuan-dengan-msci) .


She said MSCI gave no signal before the consultation opened, according to Bloomberg Technoz, which also reported that OJK investigators detained three suspects on November 16 in a warrant manipulation case.


MSCI’s release credits reforms such as a roadmap toward a 15% minimum free float, but says institutional investors want evidence of sustained impact.


People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News that MSCI chief executive Henry Fernandez told President Prabowo Subianto on a November 10 call, arranged by Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio, that he was willing to consider options other than the two-step downgrade.


Tina Tan, MSCI’s executive director of marketing and communications for Asia-Pacific, told[Bloomberg Technoz](https://www.bloombergtechnoz.com/detail-news/128379/ini-kata-msci-soal-isu-pertemuan-dengan-prabowo) that MSCI could not comment on the reported meeting and that meeting officials, regulators and exchanges is part of its standard consultation process.


## MSCI’s Timeline: Consultation Closes April 30, 2027, Decision by June 30, 2027


Date Step


January 2026 MSCI first raises the threat of a downgrade, per Bloomberg News


June 2026 Market Classification Review sets the November 2026 Index Review as the checkpoint


October 15, 2026 MSCI opens the Standalone consultation and keeps the freeze


April 30, 2027 Deadline for market participants’ feedback


June 30, 2027 MSCI announces its decision on or before this date


MSCI may give an interim update before then. Rully expects foreign funds to respond after the announcement: active investors tend to sell beforehand, while passive investors adjust only after the official decision, Liputan6 reported.


## What It Means for EIDO and Emerging-Market Funds Like EEM and VWO


EIDO tracks the MSCI Indonesia IMI 25-50 index with 60 holdings and $472.49 million in assets, led by banks such as Bank Central Asia at 22.50% and Bank Rakyat Indonesia at 14.79%, per Stock Analysis.


The[Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF (VWO)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/vwo/) follows a FTSE index instead, per[Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/vwo/) , and FTSE Russell kept Indonesia as a Secondary Emerging Market on November 13, off its Watch List, while deferring some index changes, such as new additions and free float increases, until at least its March 2027 review,[Katadata](https://katadata.co.id/finansial/bursa/6af80fc91cffa/ftse-russell-pertahankan-status-pasar-modal-indonesia-di-emerging-market) reported.
